status_detail: Ionic announced a 10-year triple-net lease of the full 234 MW Cedarvale facility capacity to Nscale for AI/HPC workloads; facility was an existing digital infrastructure/Bitcoin mining site in Ward County.
notes: Company source says Cedarvale is in Barstow, Texas, and Nscale will lease full 234 MW capacity; county website checked for local context.

project_name: Circe Energy West Texas AI Infrastructure Campus
aliases: Circe Energy Data Centers E. Monahans Campus
status_detail: Circe describes a flagship Permian/West Texas HPC campus launching with 50 MW in 2026, 150 MW in 2027 and scaling to 1.1 GW by 2030; DCD reports 1,950-acre site and phased energization planned for 2027. Oil & Gas Watch maps the associated E. Monahans campus power plant in Ward County.
notes: County placement relies on tracker/regulatory mapping for E. Monahans/Ward County; Circe's own page identifies West Texas/Permian but not the county.

project_name: Viridien Brenham Advanced Technology / HPC Facility
status_detail: City says the project has been in process for more than three years and is for Viridien's own research/technology computing, not public cloud, AI, or crypto; Brenham council reportedly rejected the tax abatement/phase-in request in January 2026, but the land was already sold and the project was not itself up for approval at that vote.
notes: DCD reports 40,000 sq ft initial building on 21 acres at 2602 Longwood Drive with possible expansion to three buildings totaling 45 MW by 2028 and up to $100M investment.

status_detail: Energy Abundance announced a 50,000-acre behind-the-meter AI data center hub near Laredo, phased from an initial 300 MW and 1M sq ft in 2026 to 5 GW and 15M+ sq ft; local Laredo/Webb officials later said no formal data center applications had been submitted to the city or county as of August 2026.
notes: Location is described as near Laredo/Webb County in secondary/tracker sources; official local applications were not found.

status_detail: Laredo Morning Times reported that a data center appeared in a Talise master plan/presentation, but the Walker family's representative said it was included without approval and removed; city and county officials reiterated that no formal application had been submitted.
notes: Included under no-miss policy because it appeared in public debate/records, but evidence points to removed concept rather than active project.

status_detail: TDLR filings show multiple Project Eagle data center buildings in Boling, Wharton County, each 189,060 sq ft and $300M, with Building A start 8/1/2026 and later buildings start 9/1/2026; local reporting says initial four buildings total about 756,240 sq ft/$1.2B and later filings expanded the campus.
notes: Also found TDLR auxiliary water building TABS2026026969 and community reports describing a roughly 2,700-acre campus; capacity not disclosed in official filings.

status_detail: No data center project body found in Wheeler County during targeted searches.
notes: Google/Intersect's Meitner data center is in Gray and Roberts Counties; Wheeler County appears only as the location of the 800-acre Caprock Workforce Hub for up to 3,500 construction workers, so it is not counted as a county data center project.

status_detail: Skybox lists PowerCampus Texas in Wichita Falls as 300+ acres with up to 2M sq ft and private onsite substations for 300+ MW; local officials announced Skybox bought 225 acres in the Wichita Falls Business Park and the first building could be operational by late 2028.
notes: Skybox page gives 300+ MW and 300+ acres; news reports cite 225-acre purchase and up to seven buildings.

project_name: Airport Drive data center rezoning proposal
developer: Undisclosed; local attorney Brad Altman represented land/development interests
status_detail: Wichita Falls City Council unanimously rejected rezoning for a possible large-scale data center near Airport Drive after tabling the item earlier; DCD previously reported the proposal could cover 98 acres with up to nine buildings and 1.35M sq ft.
notes: Rejected project included because brief counts rejected projects; exact developer and MW were not public in the sources found.

developer: Google; AES energy partner; Planton/Platon Investments filing entities
status_detail: Google announced a new air-cooled data center under construction in Wilbarger County, co-located with clean power developed by AES; TDLR filings for Project Rise 1A and Rise 2A each list FM 2897 S, Vernon, 991,000 sq ft, $500M, start 3/31/2026 and completion 3/31/2028.
notes: Two TDLR records total $1B and 1.982M sq ft; Google/AES announcement does not disclose MW capacity.

developer: Soluna Holdings / Soluna Computing; EDF Renewables energy partner; Galaxy Digital customer for Kati 1A
status_detail: Soluna says Project Kati is a 166 MW wind-powered data center campus in Willacy County; company and local reporting indicate construction/groundbreaking in 2025, first 83 MW phase targeted for early 2026, and county commissioners approved a tax abatement/PILOT for phase one.
notes: RGV Business Journal locates first site north of County Line Road and east of FM 1420 and notes first two 83 MW phases total 166 MW; later Soluna/SEC materials discuss AI/HPC expansion potential beyond Bitcoin hosting.

status_detail: City of Taylor project page describes a proposed 135,000 sq ft data center in three phases, $1B total investment, with three buildings, substation, backup generators and closed-loop cooling; local reporting says Taylor City Council approved the project in July 2024.
notes: Capacity from local reporting; Taylor official page confirms scale, use, location and phasing.

status_detail: Local reporting describes Blueprint's Georgetown sister facility off Westinghouse Road as a $160M, approximately 45,000 sq ft, 10-acre data center with up to 25 MW; zoning/incentives approved September 2024 and first phase expected operational by late 2026.
notes: County official site checked; details came from local reporting rather than a dedicated official project page found in quick search.

status_detail: Sabey's official SDC Austin page lists two purpose-built data centers in Round Rock with up to 84 MW and 603,300 sq ft; Round Rock city says the first 213,000 sq ft building was completed in fall 2024 and the campus will host TACC's Horizon supercomputer.
notes: TACC says Horizon goes into operation in 2026; Sabey page gives 84 MW and 603,300 sq ft.

status_detail: Switch announced its Fifth Prime campus next to Dell's Round Rock HQ with over 1.5M sq ft at The Rock; Round Rock city says Switch received approvals in 2021 and 2023 and is constructing at 300 Dell Way, while the combined Texas ecosystem would provide over 2M sq ft and 185 MW on completion.
notes: 185 MW is for Switch's Texas technology campus ecosystem as stated in Switch announcement, not solely one building.

status_detail: Round Rock official page says Skybox Old Settlers PUD seeks rezoning of 29.69 acres for a data center and substation; added provisions limit it to one data center building of 250,000 sq ft, 60 ft height and 75 MW grid-interconnected power, with closed-loop cooling and no incentives.
notes: City page showed first-reading approval and scheduled final vote; local TV reported final approval, so status marked approved.

status_detail: Local reporting describes the Hutto Megasite Skybox/Prologis campus on 159 acres as well underway, with nearly 4M sq ft across several buildings, at least $10B capex, and roughly 600 MW; developers secured a development agreement and Chapter 312 tax abatement in 2024.
notes: Official Hutto documents were not opened in this quick pass; include as high-priority local-news sourced item due scale.

project_name: Iron Mountain Taylor Meadows data center campus
status_detail: Iron Mountain presented a proposed approximately 500-acre data center complex on CR 404 in Taylor's ETJ, seeking Hutto wastewater service; project would include seven data center buildings with closed-loop water systems, electrical substation, utility yards, new county roads and stormwater detention.
notes: Water/sewer demand reported as 30,200 gallons per day; MW not disclosed in opened sources.

status_detail: Local reporting says Colovore won Hutto City Council approval in December 2024 for a 180,000 sq ft liquid-cooled AI/HPC colocation data center plus 13,000 sq ft office on 30 acres at 2351 Innovation Blvd; construction expected to begin in early 2026.
notes: Included to avoid missing a Hutto campus; no official city page located during the quick pass.

notes: Speculative/placeholder; listed because the PUD permits data center use but no construction plan was found.

notes: Sparse official record in the opened page; retained as an approved but not-started local project.

developer: Misae / renewable energy developer Falin-related reporting
